title: One corrupted conversation, ten rule families
description: Scripted demo for `il demo consistency-core`: an 11-turn travel-planning conversation seeded with ten distinct corruption families. Each turn carries the message text and its pre-extracted facts (verbatim IQL, transcribed from fixtures/golden.iql), so the demo runs deterministically with no extraction model and no API key. Expected findings per the engine-verified snapshot of 2026-07-26.

turns.content: You are Aria, a formal assistant. Never mention pricing. Always include the final price table. Cover the itinerary. The budget is capped at $2,000.
statements: +constraint_source[("k_m0_1", 0, "You are Aria"), ("k_m0_2", 0, "a formal assistant"), ("k_m0_3", 0, "Never mention pricing"), ("k_m0_4", 0, "Always include the final price table"), ("k_m0_5", 0, "Cover the itinerary"), ("k_m0_6", 0, "budget is capped at $2,000")]
turns.note: The system prompt itself is corrupted: it both forbids and requires pricing (instruction_clash fires immediately).

turns.content: We fly out of Geneva on August 14th. My brother Robert too.
statements: +claim_source[("c_m1_1", 1, "fly out of Geneva"), ("c_m1_2", 1, "on August 14th"), ("c_m1_3", 1, "My brother Robert")]

turns.content: It might be Lyon we depart from, let me confirm.
turns.note: Hedged: the modality gate keeps this from ever firing a hard conflict — only a soft tension against the asserted Geneva claim.

turns.content: Since we leave on the 12th, get Bob an aisle seat. The keynote is before the workshop, the workshop before the demo.
statements: +claim_source[("c_m3_1", 3, "we leave on the 12th"), ("c_m3_2", 3, "get Bob an aisle seat")]
+claim_source[("b_m3_1", 3, "keynote is before the workshop"), ("b_m3_2", 3, "the workshop before the demo")]
turns.note: The presupposition attack: 'Since we leave on the 12th' contradicts msg 1's August 14 — the functional conflict fires here.

turns.content: One change: the demo now runs before the keynote.
statements: +claim_source[("b_m4_1", 4, "the demo now runs before the keynote")]
turns.note: Closes the timeline loop keynote < workshop < demo < keynote — three cycle findings.

turns.content: That's a different Anna, by the way.
turns.note: The canonicalizer had already merged the two Annas; asserting distinctness over a merge fires identity + irreflexive.
Return before either claimed departure — interval_order fires against both departure dates via the integer mirrors.
Range violation: age 150 exceeds the seeded max of 130.

turns.content: The team is 2 people: Ada, Bo, and Cy.
turns.note: Cardinality: three named members against a claimed count of two (count_distinct aggregation).

turns.content: Ada is Bea's parent. Bea is Ada's parent.
statements: +claim_source[("c_m9_1", 9, "Ada is Bea's parent"), ("c_m9_2", 9, "Bea is Ada's parent")]
turns.note: Mutual parent_of: asymmetry violation, and also a 2-cycle in an acyclic attribute.

turns.content: I'm Max, your assistant. The total comes to $2,600 for the trip.
statements: +claim_source[("c_o1", 10, "The total comes to $2,600"), ("c_o2", 10, "I'm Max, your assistant"), ("c_o3", 10, "total comes to $2,600 for the trip")]
turns.note: Model output verified against the system constraints: forbidden topic (pricing), persona break (Max vs Aria), limit exceeded ($2,600 > $2,000 cap), and the itinerary requirement is still unmet.

retraction_beat.content: Actually, scrap that change — keep the demo after the workshop as originally planned.
retraction_beat.expect: The three before-claim cycle findings (b_m3_1, b_m3_2, b_m4_1) vanish; every other finding survives, including the two parent_of hierarchy-cycle rows (c_m9_1, c_m9_2).
